question: Should OpenClaw allow sandboxed sessions to request ACP host or worker spawns, and which security boundary should own that capability?
rationale: The code can implement several shapes, but automation should not choose whether the sandbox boundary is preserved through isolated workers, crossed through an audited host bridge, or kept closed.

options.title: Prefer Isolated ACP Workers
options.body: Extend the execution-backend/profile design so ACP can run in a sandboxed worker or sidecar with explicit auth, workspace, secret, lifecycle, and audit boundaries before enabling sandboxed requesters.

options.title: Approve Audited Host Bridge
options.body: Add an opt-in host-side ACP proxy with narrow spawn/steer/cancel APIs, allowlists, rate limits, durable audit logs, and clear operator warnings for controlled privilege crossing.

options.title: Keep Current Block
options.body: Continue documenting that sandboxed sessions must use `runtime="subagent"` or run ACP-capable harnesses inside the sandbox until a stronger design is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Prefer Isolated ACP Workers
recommendation.body: Extend the execution-backend/profile design so ACP can run in a sandboxed worker or sidecar with explicit auth, workspace, secret, lifecycle, and audit boundaries before enabling sandboxed requesters.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz merged the current ACP sandbox hardening and is the strongest history signal for the ACP runtime/security-boundary decision.
